leads.subject: 1547 Iurghiceni property chain
leads.scope: Iurghiceni on the Bahlui, Hârlău district, Moldavia, 1547–1619
leads.next_action: Recover the full 1611 document text and the 1619 cotas 24–28 originals/transcriptions. Compare exact property descriptions, neighboring owners, witnesses, prior-title language and any ancestry statements. Search Iurghiceni records between 1547 and 1611 and after 1620 for an explicit link to Cican/Illea. Treat Frim/Frimu as a separate documented person until such a link is found.
leads.notes: Primary/archival catalog evidence confirms the 1547 charter (Cican/Cicican and son Illea) and a separate 1611 Iurghiceni testimony that Frim sold his ancestral holding. Published documentary indexes then identify 1619 Iurghiceni records: Costin and Lupu receive land bought from Milrica daughter of Udrea (27 May); Costin is empowered to possess Frimu's portion because he paid 46 talers for Frimu's ransom (27 May); and on 20 June Costin/Lupu receive Iurghiceni land bought from Iosif son of Vasile Cergas and a separate portion bought from Frimu son of Bilan. A 1620 record continues Costin's possession at Iurghiceni. None of these later records currently names Cican/Illea or proves descent from them.

leads.subject: Iurghiceni 1591–1599 ownership continuity
leads.next_action: Recover the full 1611 original/transcription and determine the exact form and identity of 'Costinovici' (patronymic/house-name/person). Compare it with the 1619 Costin vistiernic and every Frimu son of Bilan reference. Then trace Costin/Costinovici and Frim's property backward and forward through Iurghiceni records. Separately recover the full 1591–1592 text and map the Cătrîna–Gavril–Ștefan–Agafia–Obrejie branch.
leads.notes: BNaR primary catalogue evidence now gives a more precise 1611 relationship: on 16 March 1611, Popa Toader and others from Iurghiceni testify that Frim son of Bilan sold his Iurghiceni ocină to his nephew Costinovici. Published 1619 records then show Costin/Costinovici-context property transactions involving Frimu son of Bilan and Iurghiceni. This establishes a documentary Frim/Frimu–Costin family/property chain, but no current source connects Frim or Costinovici to the 1547 Cican/Cicican and Illea. The 1591–1592 Iurghiceni transaction involving Ștefan son of Cătrîna and his cousin Obrejie remains a separate documented branch unless a primary text provides a bridge.

leads.title: Cicicani / Ion of Cicicani — 1638 Hotin documentary cluster
leads.scope: Cicicani near Forosna in the historical Hotin region; 26 February 1638 record names Tațea, daughter of Ion from Cicicani, as Nasta's maternal grandmother and identifies inherited property in Cicicani.
evidence: DRH A. Moldova XXII, doc. 278, pp. 311–312, as cited by secondary historical studies
Historical settlement catalogues identify Cicicani near Forosna/Novoselița
leads.next_action: Recover and compare DRH A, vol. XXIV, doc. 249 (1638) and the 1643/1645 documents; determine whether earlier Cicicani records identify Ion or his descendants and whether any record independently uses Cican/Cicican as a personal surname. Keep this cluster separate from the 1547 Cican/Cicican at Iurghiceni unless an explicit documentary bridge is found.
leads.notes: The 26 February 1638 record is independently described in scholarly historical studies as Nasta, daughter of Ivan Vartic and Tațea, daughter of Ion din Cicicani, identifying Cicicani as a property-bearing locality in the historical Hotin region near Forosna/Novoselița. Later 1643 and 1645 records continue the same Cicicani property context through Nasta/Tațea's line. The wording supports a locative designation ('Ion din Cicicani') and property inheritance, not a Cican surname identification.

leads.subject: Cicănești / Cica / possible Cican toponymic-anthroponymic connection
leads.notes: The official Cicănești local-history page confirms documentary attestation of the settlement on 11 June 1565. A secondary historical/onomastic source states that Cica is attested as a personal name in 1526 and discusses a proposed Cican-derived explanation for the place-name. This does not establish that the 1547 Moldavian Cican/Cicican or the user's family originated in Cicănești.
leads.next_action: Recover the 1526 personal-name citation and the 1565 primary charter; determine the exact historical spelling and grammatical form of the place-name and personal name; search intervening and surrounding Wallachian records for Cica/Cican/Cicănești variants; compare chronology and geography without assuming identity or origin.

leads.subject: Iurghiceni 1611 Frim son of Bilan → Costinovici → 1619 Costin/Frimu property chain
leads.hypothesis: The 1611 sale by Frim son of Bilan to his nephew Costinovici may be connected to the Costin/Frimu property transactions documented in 1619 and later Iurghiceni records.
leads.notes: BNaR's 1611 inventory explicitly says Frim son of Bilan sold his Iurghiceni ocină to his nephew Costinovici. The 1619 BNaR inventory says Costin vistiernicul of Iurghiceni received an ocină purchased from Frimu son of Bălan for 46 silver talers; the 1620 document confirms Costin's Iurghiceni holding. A 1632 scholarly edition independently records Costin's Iurghiceni holding and local witnesses. These records strengthen the Costin/Frim documentary chain, but do not connect it to Cican/Cicican/Illea.
leads.next_action: Recover and compare the 1611 original/transcription with the 1619 I/27 document and 1620 I/28; resolve whether Costinovici and Costin vistiernicul are the same individual or related individuals. Extend through 1622 and 1632 records. Search backward for Frim son of Bilan's title, parentage and acquisition language.
